proposals.location: Algorithm 1, PDF pp.6–7; modified density threshold; Lemma3.8
schedule: Rounds1–2: exchange identifiers then neighbor lists; decide phase-one set D using adjacencies from N(v) to candidate vertices in N²(v).
Round3: broadcast D membership; each vertex knows whether it lies in N[D].
Round4: broadcast uncovered flags; each vertex computes residual closed-neighborhood degree.
Round5: broadcast residual degrees; each uncovered vertex chooses its dominator.
Round6: notify selected neighbors; all vertices know final membership.

gen-w25-dom.proof: Six LOCAL flooding rounds reveal neighbor lists and degrees through distance five. They determine phase-one membership through distance three and uncovered status through distance two around a selecting vertex v. Every candidate replacing beta(v) must cover v, since v belongs to the required uncovered neighborhood; hence that candidate lies in N[v]. One final notification round determines output membership. This is a conservative upper bound, not a printed or optimal count.
